channel.title: NRBC Compliance Brief
channel.description: A daily morning brief from New Realm Brewing on alcohol and hemp/THC regulation — TTB and state actions, hemp THC beverage rules, tariffs, court decisions and enforcement. Federal and all 50 states.

item.title: Connecticut cannabis tax overhaul takes effect tomorrow — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 48 (Sep 30, 2026)
item.description: Connecticut's flat 10.75% cannabis tax and higher THC beverage limits take effect tomorrow. Also: TTB: third-quarter CBMA import refund claims open Thursday, October 1; Coors Distributing sues Constellation and Mark Anthony in civil court to block terminations

item.title: Pennsylvania senator proposes statewide hemp-THC framework — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 47 (Sep 29, 2026)
item.description: Pennsylvania Senator Unveils Statewide Hemp-THC Regulation Framework. Also: Federal Judge Dismisses Patco Brands' Final Counterclaims Against BuzzBallz; Sixth Circuit Narrows Injunction Against Ohio's Hemp-THC Restrictions. Daily alcohol and hemp/THC regulatory brief — federal and all 50 states.

item.title: Massachusetts voters oppose cannabis-sales repeal, poll finds — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 46 (Sep 28, 2026)
item.description: Massachusetts voters oppose ballot measure to repeal cannabis sales, 71–24, new poll finds. Also: Last day to enter Canadian alcohol: import exclusion takes effect at 12:01 a.m. Tuesday; Pennsylvania House speaker says cannabis legalization is possible next year, contingent on November elections

item.title: Denver distributor contests Constellation, Mark Anthony terminations — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 45 (Sep 27, 2026)
item.description: Denver's Coors Distributing says it plans to fight Constellation and Mark Anthony terminations. Also: Sen. Scott files amendment barring college-athlete NIL deals that promote alcohol or cannabis; Massachusetts governor proposes veteran medical cannabis cards on VA documentation, tax-free purchases

item.title: Montana ties cannabis licenses to resident control — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 44 (Sep 26, 2026)
item.description: Montana ties cannabis licenses to resident operational control, effective today. Also: Arizona attorney general sues Feel Free maker Botanic Tonics under consumer fraud law; Pennsylvania Senate panel takes up adult-use legalization as two bills sit pending

item.title: Canadian packaged-alcohol import ban takes effect Monday — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 43 (Sep 25, 2026)
item.description: Import ban on Canadian packaged alcohol takes effect Monday at 12:01 a.m. Also: Senate amendment would bar student-athlete deals promoting alcohol, marijuana and gambling; Nebraska attorney general says he won't keep challenging the medical cannabis law

item.title: GAO flags gaps in federal drug scheduling process — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 42 (Sep 24, 2026)
item.description: GAO finds “gaps” in DEA and FDA drug scheduling procedures as marijuana rescheduling review continues. Also: 59-group alcohol coalition asks for a permanent U.S.–Canada deal before the September 29 import exclusion; New House bill would treat alcohol and cannabis as “high-risk” ad categories requiri

item.title: Maryland drafts new cannabis licensing rules — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 40 (Sep 23, 2026)
item.description: Maryland drafts wide-ranging cannabis rule changes, tying license renewals to tax compliance. Also: Two-thirds of Missouri cannabis operators skipped DEA registration under rescheduling — and none who applied are approved yet; Minnesota liquor retailers report THC beverage growth heading into Decemb

item.title: North Carolina panel floats state-run cannabis retail — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 39 (Sep 22, 2026)
item.description: North Carolina panel floats state-run cannabis stores, private cultivation licenses. Also: Fourth Circuit panel questions DEA’s Schedule I designation of hemp-derived HHC; California cannabis chief: DEA has issued no rescheduling implementation guidance to states

item.title: Texas defends hemp license fees in appeals court — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 38 (Sep 21, 2026)
item.description: Texas defends hemp product rules — including per-location license fees — in appeals court filing. Also: North Carolina poll: majority backs keeping hemp THC products legal for adults 21 and over; Delaware governor signs bill adding marijuana to alcohol enforcement division's name and mandate

item.title: Ohio brewers seek beer franchise law overhaul — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 37 (Sep 20, 2026)
item.description: Craft brewers press Ohio Senate to overhaul the state's 1974 beer franchise law. Also: New York moves delinquent cannabis retailers to cash-on-delivery as unpaid supplier bills reach $3.9 million; Missouri recalls infused pre-rolls after aspergillus test failure, its second recall this month

item.title: Michigan revokes cannabis license, sets record fine — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 36 (Sep 19, 2026)
item.description: Michigan revokes Muha Meds maker's license, imposes record $2 million fine. Also: Alabama health committee withdraws objection to federal marijuana rescheduling; Massachusetts opens major overhaul of cannabis rules, including new license types

item.title: Appeals court weighs Illinois wine shipping ban — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 35 (Sep 18, 2026)
item.description: Seventh Circuit hears challenge to Illinois ban on out-of-state wine shipments. Also: Bipartisan bill would shield insurers that cover state-licensed cannabis businesses; Colorado expands residual-solvent testing; issues two contamination advisories

item.title: Supreme Court asked to review licensing residency rules — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 34 (Sep 17, 2026)
item.description: U.S. Supreme Court asked to decide whether states may favor residents in cannabis licensing. Also: House passes Tyler's Law, directing HHS study of ER drug testing that includes marijuana; Federal Reserve flags enhanced anti-money-laundering expectations for banks serving cannabis businesses

item.title: Pennsylvania charges 12 over store-sold THC products — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 33 (Sep 16, 2026)
item.description: Pennsylvania charges 12 in $18.7 million THC trafficking case tied to convenience stores. Also: Bipartisan group of senators reintroduces SAFE Banking Act; Texas hemp fees, the full schedule: $5,000 per retail location, $10,000 per manufacturing location

item.title: Ban on Canadian alcohol imports begins September 29 — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 32 (Sep 15, 2026)
item.description: Proclamation excludes Canadian packaged alcohol from U.S. importation starting September 29. Also: Companion proclamation revises the 50% Canada duty list, effective today; New York official signals enforcement against unlicensed hemp THC beverage sales

item.title: Southern Glazer's pays $12.5M to settle bribery probe — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 31 (Sep 14, 2026)
item.description: Southern Glazer’s to pay $12.5 million to resolve federal bribery investigation. Also: Trump says he will remove the 10% tariff on Irish whiskey; Sixth Circuit reverses $31.8M verdict, holds marijuana contracts unenforceable in federal court

item.title: Constellation to exit Coors Distributing in Colorado — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 30 (Sep 13, 2026)
item.description: Constellation Brands portfolio to exit Coors Distributing Company in Colorado. Also: Dispensary owner says DEA registration conditions require removing employees with felony drug convictions; Illinois licenses 37 adult-use dispensaries to serve medical cannabis patients

item.title: Nebraska high court rejects medical cannabis challenge — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 29 (Sep 12, 2026)
item.description: Nebraska Supreme Court rejects constitutional challenge to voter-approved medical cannabis laws. Also: DEA registration conditions under Schedule III come into focus, including employment screening; Georgia: medical cannabis patients may now vaporize — but not smoke — under expanded law

item.title: Southern Glazer's pays $12.5M in trade-practice settlement — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 28 (Sep 11, 2026)
item.description: Southern Glazer's to pay $12.5 million to resolve federal bribery and false-invoicing investigation. Also: Census Bureau: states collected $15.8 billion in marijuana tax revenue over five years; Connecticut: federal judge dismisses hemp farmers' challenge to state THC restrictions
